classification.difficultyReason: Select squared and cubed scale laws in opposite directions and convert cubic metres to cubic centimetres before division.

content.prompt: A model car has scale $1:24$; that is, $1\text{ cm}$ on the model represents $24\text{ cm}$ on the actual car.

children.label: a
children.prompt: If the model car requires $300\text{ cm}^2$ of material to be made, how much material is required to make the actual car?

answer.worked:
The actual car's lengths are $24$ times the model's lengths, so its surface area is $24^2$ times as large.

$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{actual}}&=300\times24^2\\A_{\text{actual}}&=172\,800\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: If the volume of the actual car's interior is $4.5\text{ m}^3$, find the volume of the model's interior, in $\text{cm}^3$ and correct to one decimal place.

answer.worked:
The model's volume is $\dfrac{1}{24^3}$ of the actual car's volume.

$$\begin{align*}V_{\text{actual}}&=4.5\times100^3\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{actual}}&=4\,500\,000\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&=\frac{4\,500\,000}{24^3}\text{ cm}^3\\V_{\text{model}}&\approx325.5\text{ cm}^3\end{align*}$$
